_comment: Worked example only (the demo build: the baby-eczema run, which used the villain-arc story shape — the problem as a cartoon villain narrating its own defeat; brand name, product and URL replaced with placeholders). The villain arc is ONE story option, not the format: a new run's scenes follow whatever choices.story_shape and choices.cast the user picked. Creative fields — scenes[].caption (wording follows choices.story_shape + choices.narrator), scenes[].vo (choices.narrator + choices.narrator_voice), scenes[].clip (choices.visual_style + choices.cast), music_bed (choices.music), end_card.wordmark/product_line/claims/cta and brand_palette (the user's brand) — come from the recipe's choices and brand inputs; never copy them as defaults. No cure claims in captions or end-card copy. The recipe binds a NEW brand's own clips / VO / product / palette / copy here. Every path is a placeholder to REPLACE with an absolute path or a runtime working/ path. `target_sec` per scene is the MEASURED VO window (ffprobe each VO mp3 — never a planned word count). Scene order follows the recipe's neutral beat slots (hook: the problem -> teach the mechanism -> what it costs -> the product arrives -> CLIMAX: the fix -> payoff); the end card is a SEPARATE block (built by build_endcard.py), not a scene. end_card.vo is OPTIONAL: the path to the end card's spoken line. It plays from the start of the end-card window, and the dwell becomes the larger of dwell_sec and the line's duration + 0.5s. Remove the key for a silent end card.

Its pH lock snaps it back to 4.9
Calm baby. Nowhere left to live.
